comment: GENERATED-BY-HAND definition; the RESULT beside it is recorded by scripts/mutate_campaign.py --run and the counts are derived from it, never typed.
description: #262 Stage 2 — the CI/dogfood ENGINE-SELECTION seam. Stage 2's deliverable is a configuration, so its mutants are configuration: each one is a plausible way the Rust-default claim could quietly stop being true, or the public contract could quietly start moving, while every job still went green. The catchers are the controls in tests/test_stage2_dogfood.py, which read the workflows rather than being told about them.
layers_comment: One layer, on Linux, and that is a claim rather than a convenience. Every mutation here targets DECLARATIVE text — a workflow key, a ledger entry, a C# constant, an action input — and every catcher reads that text, so the verdict is identical on either platform. This is not the Stage-1 situation, where mutants of scripts/own-check.ps1 changed PowerShell SEMANTICS that only a Windows runtime can evaluate; those keep their Windows-native campaign (p022-stage1-windows) and this one does not inherit their requirement. The one Stage-2 mutation with a platform dimension, S03, deletes the windows-latest leg from the matrix — and deleting it is exactly what a Windows runner could not report.

control.description: harness-honesty control: no mutation at all, which must report zero failing layers

mutations.description: the dog-food job stops asking for an engine — the most likely regression of all, because the job still runs, still analyses, still uploads, and silently goes back to the public Python default
mutations.pattern: engine: rust               # STAGE 2: the dogfood runs on the Rust core

mutations.description: the dog-food candidate becomes own-shadow-engine — the #260 dev adapter is a Rust binary that this repository really builds, so the substitution looks right and measures a thing that is not the product
the Rust-default dogfood matrix loses its Windows leg — 'our CI runs on Rust' quietly becomes a statement about Linux, which is the half of the product whose launcher mechanics never broke
mutations.pattern:
name: Rust-default dogfood \(Own\.NET's own tree, via own-cli\)
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: \[ubuntu-latest, windows-latest\]
mutations.replacement:
name: Rust-default dogfood (Own.NET's own tree, via own-cli)
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]

mutations.description: the dogfood finds its candidate on PATH — 'the binary is right there, why spell out an absolute path', which is precisely how a stale binary stands in for the one under test
the dogfood run swallows its exit code — the classic 'don't let the dogfood job break the build', which turns every Rust-default claim in this PR into decoration
mutations.replacement: out=$(bash scripts/own-check.sh --engine rust --format human --fail-on-finding -- frontend/roslyn/samples || true)

mutations.description: the PRODUCT default flips to Rust — the covert Stage 3, and the single edit that would make every internal Rust job pass by accident while changing what every user gets
the ACTION's public engine input defaults to rust — the same cutover through the other public door, and the one a C#-only control would miss
a #260 compare gate is disabled — the cheapest way to make a Rust-default dogfood green is to remove the job that would have disagreed with it
mutations.replacement:
shadow-compare:
    name: shadow compare (committed corpus)
    if: false

mutations.description: a new bare launcher invocation appears in a job nobody classified — the hole the census exists to close, and the one that reopens every time somebody adds a convenient scan step
mutations.pattern: - name: Check the emitted method is still in sync with the golden host
mutations.replacement:
- name: Check the emitted method is still in sync with the golden host
        run: scripts/own-check.sh --format human -- frontend/roslyn/samples

mutations.description: the dog-food job is reclassified out of the Rust-default population — every other rule is satisfied by shrinking Class D, so without a rule that reads the job's own name this is a green way to stop dogfooding

the dog-food's engine selection is COMMENTED OUT rather than deleted — the shape a temporary rollback really takes ('just for one run, we'll put it back'). Its twin S01 deletes the line; this one leaves the words `engine: rust` sitting in the file, which is all a control that greps the job's raw text would need to stay green. It exists because S03 survived for exactly that reason on a different key
mutations.pattern: engine: rust               # STAGE 2: the dogfood runs on the Rust core
mutations.replacement: # engine: rust             # STAGE 2: the dogfood runs on the Rust core
